alerts.headline: EMERGENCY ALERT - FLOODING
alerts.description:
CIVIL DEFENCE - FLOODING
Heavy rain is causing flooding in parts of Ōhura town, Ruapehu District. Life-threatening flooding is possible. 
PREPARE TO EVACUATE from low-lying areas near Mangaroa Stream and other catchments. 
IF YOU FEEL UNSAFE, LEAVE IMMEDIATELY. 
A civil Defence centre is available at the Memorial Hall, 15 Ngarimu Street, Ohura. 
People in low-lying areas should:
•	Follow instructions from emergency services 
•      Prepare a bag with essential items 
•      Organise to stay with family or friends if they can 
•	Take your pets with you
•      Check on neighbours and anyone who may need help
•      Share this information if it won't delay you
DO NOT WALK OR DRIVE THROUGH FLOOD WATERS. 
Flood water may be contaminated and contain debris.
For more information, visit www.civildefence.govt.nz
Issued on behalf of Manawatū-Whanganui CDEM Group by NEMA

alerts.headline: CIVIL DEFENCE WARNING - FLOODING
alerts.description:
CIVIL DEFENCE WARNING - FLOODING

Heavy rain in the upper reaches of the Whanganui River, combined with high tide, is forecast to bring possible flooding to Anzac Parade, Taupo Quay, and the Putiki suburb around 1pm. 

PEOPLE SHOULD PREPARE TO EVACUATE from those areas. Civil Defence staff are commencing door knocking in these areas.
 
IF YOU FEEL UNSAFE, LEAVE IMMEDIATELY. 

People in low-lying areas should:
*Follow instructions from emergency services and Civil Defence
*Prepare a bag with essential items 
*Organise to stay with family or friends if they can 
*Take your pets with you
*Check on neighbours and anyone who may need help
*Share this information if it won't delay you 

DO NOT WALK OR DRIVE THROUGH FLOOD WATERS. 
Flood water may be contaminated and contain debris.

For more information, visit www.mwcdem.govt.nz
Issued by Manawatu-Whanganui CDEM Group

alerts.sender_name: Manawatu-Whanganui Civil Defence Emergency Management Group
alerts.headline: CIVIL DEFENCE WARNING - FLOODING
alerts.description:
UPDATE 2:05PM SUNDAY 19 APRIL

Whanganui District Council Civil Defence staff have advised no mandatory evacuations are required as a result of the high river level. However, residents in low-lying areas should remain vigilant.

Thank you for taking this situation seriously and being prepared. It is always better to be prepared in these situations than to leave it too late. 

River levels will remain high for some time, with areas such as the Taupo Quay boardwalk to experience some inundation.

DO NOT WALK OR DRIVE THROUGH FLOOD WATERS. Flood water may be contaminated and contain debris.

Various roads remain closed. Continue to follow instructions from emergency services and Civil Defence staff.

For more information, visit www.mwcdem.govt.nz
Issued by Manawatu-Whanganui CDEM Group

alerts.sender_name: Wellington Civil Defence Emergency Management Group
alerts.headline: CIVIL DEFENCE SEVERE WEATHER AND FLOOD WARNING: Wairarapa
alerts.description:
CIVIL DEFENCE SEVERE WEATHER AND FLOOD WARNING: Wairarapa

Heavy rain is causing rivers and streams to rise rapidly overnight.

If you live in low lying areas, coastal settlements, or areas prone to flooding, take extra precautions and be prepared to evacuate quickly if you see signs of potential flooding.

- Consider evacuating now.
- If you see rising flood water evacuate immediately to higher ground. DO NOT WAIT for an official warning. 
- If you need to evacuate, seek shelter with friends and family if you can. Take pets and essential items.
- Call 111 if your life or property is at risk. Emergency services could be delayed.

Refer to the following websites for updates and information about Emergency Assistance Centres:
Mstn.govt.nz
Cdc.govt.nz
Swdc.govt.nz

Issued by Wellington Region Emergency Management 920pm 20/04/26

alerts.headline: FLOOD WARNING - HERBERTVILLE
alerts.description:
CIVIL DEFENCE FLOOD WARNING:  There is the potential for sudden flooding at Herbertville from the Wainui River, which has suddenly risen upstream of Herbertville.

PEOPLE SHOULD PREPARE TO EVACUATE from low-lying areas, such as the campground.

IF YOU FEEL UNSAFE, LEAVE IMMEDIATELY.

People in low-lying areas should:
- Follow instructions from emergency services and Civil Defence
- Prepare a bag with essential items
- Organise to stay with family or friends if they can
- Take your pets with you
- Check on neighbours and anyone who may need help

Share this information if it won't delay you. People can go to the Herbertville Community Hall at 43 Seaview Rd.

DO NOT WALK OR DRIVE THROUGH FLOOD WATERS. Flood water may be contaminated and contain debris.

For more information, visit www.mwcdem.govt.nz. Issued by Manawatu-Whanganui Emergency Management Group.

note: Emergency Mobile Alerts broadcast nationally in the window. The two from the Wellington CDEM Group cover Wairarapa, not Wellington city. No mobile alert went out over the city on 20 April, so absence of an alert here says nothing about conditions on a given street.
